snapshot.text: A public system pursuing universal health coverage, with a digital, primary-care-focused reform. Recurrent medicine shortages at the Central Pharmacy and pressure on social funds are the main problems; the 2027 health budget rises by 9%.

priorities.title: Medicine supply and a strategic stock
priorities.text: An emergency plan aims to restore medicine supply and build a strategic stock, after a review of the Central Pharmacy's situation in a ministerial council.

priorities.title: Universal coverage and a National Health Charter
priorities.text: The ministry signed a charter with Japan, WHO and the World Bank to support universal health coverage; commitments go to a summit in Tokyo in December 2026.

priorities.title: Budget 2027, equity and infrastructure
priorities.text: The 2027 health budget is about 6.04 billion dinars (+9%); the minister's lines are equity in health and bringing services closer to citizens, with projects such as the King Salman hospital in Kairouan (due 2029); 4,000 health staff are to be recruited in 2027.

netherlands.text: A 2014 triangular programme, signed by the Dutch minister with a Tunisian counterpart, addressed maternal mortality and family planning in Mali and Yemen.

institutions.name: Observatoire national des maladies nouvelles et émergentes

timeline.text: Joint health projects with France move into the operational phase.
Emergency plan to restore medicine supply and build a strategic stock.
At the World Health Assembly, Tunisia calls for a united African voice in global health governance reform.
Construction of the King Salman hospital in Kairouan starts; opening planned for 2029.
Cairo Declaration launches an Arab strategy 2026-2030 on health professionals abroad.
Health budget 2027 presented to parliament: about 6.04 billion dinars, up 9%.
